scene.note: Every function says in its def line what it takes and gives back, and the season closes on a sorted report.

steps.note: A list of hours goes in.
One number comes out: the total.
Next winter's reader sees both from the def line alone.
Dougie's function says it takes text, and it is always given hours of the day.
Python runs it all the same: nothing checks what the def line says.
Once its notes say what is really there, nobody reading it is misled.
A call sign is looked up among the season's leaders.
A known team gives its leader, and an unknown one gives nothing at all.
The reader can tell from the def line that the answer may be nothing.
The season's records come in with a rule that answers yes or no for one record.
The rule is asked about each record in turn.
The records it said yes to come back as a new list, in their order.
Each line of the season's file holds one callout.
Each line becomes a Callout, its hours a real number.
Rhona gets the longest callouts first, the older first where hours are equal.
